clue.text: 6 of 22 not repeatedly wanting trouble

indicators.note: the clue number 6 stands for the answer to 6-down, a word meaning jumbled, so it tells us to rearrange the letters that follow

parts.note: taken as written
22 stands for the answer to 22-down, the adjective for the skull

indicators.note: repeatedly says the little word not is taken twice over

explanation.surface: A cryptic numerical riddle about someone who keeps saying no and is spoiling for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 6 (6-down, meaning jumbled) is the anagram signal; 22 stands for the answer to 22-down, used as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone combative and spoiling for a fight is described as aggressive in this way, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Shifted rock with outside of trainer to reveal insect

indicators.note: with the outside of a word means that word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a coach is a sports trainer

indicators.note: shifted means the letters of rock are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone moves a stone with the edge of their sports shoe and finds a bug underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trainer' suggests a sports shoe in the surface, but it means a sports coach; 'Shifted' rearranges the rock.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockroach is a familiar household pest, an example of an insect.

clue.text: Wipes raised surfaces surrounding island in empty kitchen

indicators.note: surrounding says the word for raised surfaces goes round the rest

parts.note: the nap of fabric is its raised pile, so raised surfaces are naps

indicators.note: in says the island letter sits inside the emptied kitchen
empty means the word is hollowed out, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Cleaning cloths wipe raised worktops around an island unit in a bare kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised surfaces' is not worktops but the nap, the raised pile on fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Table napkins are cloths used to wipe the mouth and fingers, so they are wipes as a noun.

clue.text: See 11
Negative response three out of four bridge players doubled is rubbish

parts.note: no is the plain negative answer

indicators.note: doubled says those three letters come twice, as a bid is doubled in bridge

parts.words: three out of four bridge players
parts.note: bridge players are named North, South, East and West; three of them give N, S and E

explanation.surface: A refusal from most of a bridge table, doubled, is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubled' is bridge jargon dressed up as the repeat signal for NSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense and rubbish are both everyday words for foolish talk or worthless ideas, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Plug gaping hole off course

parts.note: a plug is an advertisement, an ad
a rift is a wide crack or split

explanation.surface: Someone tries to block a gaping hole in a boat that has drifted off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' looks like a verb meaning to stop up the hole; it is a noun, the publicity kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that is drifting with no control has wandered away from its intended route.

clue.text: Hear 7 lines in 13 books jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: lines means one thing forms a lining inside another, so these letters go within the word for heart

parts.note: 13 stands for 13-across, the organ in the chest; its synonym core means the centre of anything

indicators.note: 7 stands for 7-down, the phrase not half, so only half of the word hear is kept

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A garbled instruction to hear a few lines from a cluster of books.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers stand for answers: 7-down says take hear 'not half', and 13-across is replaced by a synonym meaning centre. 'Jumbled' looks like an anagram signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech that is incoherent is muddled and makes no sense, as jumbled words would.

clue.text: Very much what one would expect from an unfair split

definitions.meaning: the British exclamation meaning absolutely, very much so

definitions.text: what one would expect from an unfair split
definitions.meaning: an unfair split gives one party less than half

explanation.walkthrough: The British exclamation 'not half!' means 'very much so'; read literally, it is what an unequal division leaves someone with.
explanation.definitionFit: In British speech this exclamation is an emphatic yes, meaning extremely; literally it describes a share smaller than fifty per cent.

clue.text: Allow housing association's case to be listed

indicators.note: housing means the word for allow holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to let is to allow

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A tenant asks to be allowed to have a housing association's case put on the register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listed' is the nautical sense: a ship that lists leans to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that listed tilted to one side, so it inclined, the past tense of the verb meaning to tilt.

clue.text: Beat twice without beginning to increase lead

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the two synonyms go round the letter

parts.note: beat is read twice: to cap is to beat or outdo, and to tan is to beat or thrash

indicators.note: beginning to picks just the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A musician beats a drum twice, but without warming up first, to boost the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' gives two synonyms, CAP and TAN, and 'without' means outside them goes I, the start of 'increase'.
explanation.definitionFit: To captain a team is to lead it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Is this really an ingredient of haricot tagine?

indicators.note: ingredient of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diner doubts that an Italian cheese belongs in a bean stew from North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The question doubles as the definition: the soft cheese really is an 'ingredient', hidden in the words haricot tagine.
explanation.definitionFit: The question asks about a food that sits inside a dish, and the hidden cheese is literally contained in the two dish words.

clue.text: Force into performing tracks in Las Vegas

definitions.meaning: to coerce or pressure someone into doing something hastily
the American word for a train line, as found in a US city

explanation.surface: Someone is pressured into doing a show on a gambling city's stages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tracks in Las Vegas' just signals the American word for a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a railway by this word, and as a verb it means to push someone into action against their will.

clue.text: Muscle complaint

explanation.definitionFit: Informally it means muscular strength, and as slang it also means a grumble or grievance.

clue.text: Listen to opening of toccata for organ

parts.note: to hear is to listen to

indicators.note: opening of picks only the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A music student is told to listen to the start of a toccata written for organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' looks like the instrument for the toccata; it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart is the body's blood pump, an example of an internal organ.

clue.text: Sneak into enemy camp and learn if it's prepared to accept end to conflict

indicators.note: to accept means to take a letter in, so it goes inside the shuffled letters
prepared means the letters are worked up into a new form
end to picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A spy slips into the enemy camp to find out whether it is ready to agree to a ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'it' is a link ('is'); 'prepared' rearranges LEARN IF IT, which then takes in T, the end of 'conflict'.
explanation.definitionFit: To infiltrate is to get secretly into an organisation or territory, here an enemy base.

clue.text: Fear son is trying to apprehend criminal

indicators.note: to apprehend is to seize, so the words grab a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A worried parent fears their son is trying to catch a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apprehend' suggests arrest, but it means the words 'Fear son is trying' hold the answer within them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets fires deliberately commits a crime, an example of a criminal.

clue.text: Swindles in US Government associated with First Amendment

indicators.note: an amendment is a change, so the letters of the word are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Political scams in the US government tied up with the constitutional right to free speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Amendment' is the US constitutional clause on free speech; here 'Amendment' rearranges FIRST.
explanation.definitionFit: Grifts is American slang for con tricks or scams, so it means swindles in US usage.

clue.text: Hold forth a piece of cake in form of bar

parts.note: to hold forth is to speak at length
a piece of cake is an idiom for something easy

explanation.surface: A speaker talks at length while holding a slice of cake in the shape of a chocolate bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of cake' is the idiom for easy, not a baked treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A speakeasy was an illicit drinking den in Prohibition-era America, a kind of bar.

clue.text: Bard potentially starts to redefine theatre with Macbeth's opening lines

indicators.note: potentially says the letters could form a word, once they are rearranged
starts to picks the first letter of each following word, the play's name included

parts.note: the opening lines are simply lines, the word itself; opening repeats the idea of starts in the surface

explanation.surface: A would-be playwright sets out to reinvent drama, opening with Macbeth's famous lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bard' suggests Shakespeare, who fits the Macbeth surface, but it simply means a poet-singer; 'potentially' rearranges R, T, M and LINES.
explanation.definitionFit: A minstrel was a medieval singer and poet, and bard is a word for such a poet.

clue.text: Arrogance of British leaving rubbish all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means the remaining letters are scattered into a new order
leaving means that letter goes out of the word

explanation.surface: The arrogance of Britons who leave litter strewn everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving' removes B from RUBBISH to give RUBISH, which 'all over the place' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubris is excessive pride or self-confidence, a near synonym of arrogance.

clue.text: Open up highway through Scottish mountain

indicators.note: through means the road passes through the mountain, sitting inside it

parts.note: ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
a road is a highway

explanation.surface: Engineers open up a highway cutting through a Scottish peak.
explanation.definitionFit: To broaden is to widen, to open something up to more scope.

clue.text: Tip salt into wooden box

indicators.note: into says the salt goes inside the wood
box means enclose, so the wood surrounds the salt

parts.note: pine is a timber, so wooden suggests the word pine
NaCl, sodium chloride, is the chemical formula for common salt

explanation.surface: Pour salt into a wooden box, perhaps for storage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like an instruction to pour; it is the noun, the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is the highest point or peak, the very tip of a spire or mountain.

clue.text: Bend back nail, messing with the inside of one's head

indicators.note: back says the word for bend is read from right to left

parts.note: an arc is a bend or curve

indicators.note: messing with means the letters are disturbed and put in another order

explanation.surface: Someone bends a nail back and fiddles with the inside of their own skull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns ARC into CRA; 'messing with' rearranges NAIL into NIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranial means relating to the skull or cranium, so it describes things belonging to the head.

clue.text: Regularly harms one's brat, being confined to a single cell

definitions.text: being confined to a single cell

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter at even intervals

explanation.surface: A parent regularly hurts their child, who ends up locked in solitary confinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a noun here, a creature, and 'confined to a single cell' means single-celled.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a microscopic organism consisting of just one cell, a living creature of one cell.

clue.text: Unpleasant woman's right to be defended by solicitor

indicators.note: to be defended by means to be held and protected inside

parts.note: a tout is someone who solicits custom, a solicitor in that sense

explanation.surface: A disagreeable woman claims her right to be represented by a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a British lawyer; here it means one who solicits, a tout. 'Old trout' is British slang for a bad-tempered woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a trout, often an old trout, is an ill-tempered or disagreeable woman.

clue.text: Droning noise cut short president holding forth in the end

indicators.note: holding means the shortened name holds a letter inside it
cut short means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Donald Trump was US president

indicators.note: in the end picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A droning sound is abruptly halted when the president holds forth at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' takes P off TRUMP, which then holds H, the end of 'forth'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrum is a continuous low humming sound, like a droning noise.

clue.text: Screen request to get married first

indicators.note: first says the married letter is put in front

parts.note: to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A screening request: get married first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' is a verb meaning to hide, not a check.
explanation.definitionFit: To mask something is to screen or conceal it from view.

clue.text: Plant high fliers go after, wanting to prosecute

parts.note: larks are birds famous for singing high in the sky

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so that word is removed

parts.note: to pursue is to go after
to sue is to take legal action, to prosecute

explanation.surface: High fliers chase a plant, though unwilling to take legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' means lacking: PURSUE without SUE leaves PUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden flower related to the delphinium, an example of a plant.

clue.text: See 26
Shed light on collecting data I lost

indicators.note: collecting means the outer word gathers the other letters inside it

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: lost means the letters wander out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone sheds light on gathering data that they have mislaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' rearranges DATA I into ADIAT, which RE collects.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate light is to give it out or emit it, which is to shed light.

clue.text: Copy is returned after chief accountant replaces editor

indicators.note: replaces means one abbreviation is swapped in for the other

parts.note: to return a remark is to reply, so returned gives replied
CA is a chartered accountant, used here as chief accountant

explanation.surface: A copy is sent back after a chief accountant takes over from the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' means answered, giving REPLIED, whose ED is replaced by CA.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact copy or reproduction of something.

clue.text: Automotive event involved clean motor demonstration

indicators.note: involved means intricate and tangled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: a rally is a mass protest or demonstration

explanation.surface: A car show involving a demonstration of a clean engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' rearranges CLEAN MOTOR; the Monte Carlo Rally is the famous motor race in Monaco.
explanation.definitionFit: The Monte Carlo Rally is a long-running motoring competition, an example of an automotive event.
